record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Connection between layered memory and TSLV
record.original_question: Can a PDE model with both short-term and long-term memory layers be meaningfully related to the empirically motivated notion of time since last visit (TSLV)? More precisely, does including both memory compartments improve predictive power relative to models that have only one memory compartment?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 33. Can this idea of short and long-term memory be meaningfully connected to the concept of time since last visit (TSLV) as explored in [69]? More precisely, does a model featuring both short- and long-term memory components provide better predictive power than models with only one memory compartment?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a class of partial differential equation (PDE) models for animal movement in which the population density u(x,t) on a spatial domain Ω evolves under advection–diffusion dynamics whose drift term depends on internal "memory maps" carried by the animals. Specifically, allow the model to include one or two memory compartments:

(a) a short-term memory field m_S(x,t) that decays on a fast timescale τ_S and is reinforced by recent occupancy of location x;
(b) a long-term memory field m_L(x,t) that decays on a slow timescale τ_L ≫ τ_S and accumulates over longer histories of occupancy.

The animals' movement is biased by a (possibly weighted) combination of ∇m_S and ∇m_L. Separately, given an observed (or simulated) trajectory of an animal, define the time-since-last-visit field TSLV(x,t) as the elapsed time since the animal was most recently within a fixed neighborhood of x (with TSLV(x,t) = t if no prior visit has occurred).

Questions:
1. Establish a precise mathematical correspondence between the layered memory variables (m_S, m_L) of the PDE model and the empirical quantity TSLV. For instance, identify conditions (choices of reinforcement kernels and decay rates) under which functionals of (m_S(x,t), m_L(x,t)) recover TSLV(x,t) as a deterministic limit, or under which TSLV serves as a sufficient statistic for the memory state.
2. For a fitting/prediction framework where models are calibrated to movement data, determine whether the two-compartment model (with both m_S and m_L) achieves strictly better predictive performance than the one-compartment analogue (with only m_S or only m_L) — i.e., quantify the gain in predictive likelihood, identifiability of the additional parameters, and the regimes of behavioral data (e.g., foraging, territorial revisitation) in which the two-compartment structure is necessary.
artifact.category_tag: memory-driven PDE models in movement ecology
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on memory-driven animal movement (e.g., step-selection analyses with short- and long-term occurrence distributions, and PDE models with memory-based diffusion) discusses both TSLV-type covariates and layered memory, but no work was found that rigorously links the two-compartment PDE memory framework to TSLV or quantifies its predictive advantage over single-compartment models. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Identifying signals of memory from observations of animal movements
status_evidence.snippet: Memory-informed step-selection analyses include covariates such as how long ago the animal visited a location, and weights are fit for short-term and long-term memory.
status_evidence.claim: TSLV-type covariates and weighted short/long-term memory are studied empirically but the PDE linkage remains a research direction.

status_evidence.title: Detecting seasonal episodic-like spatiotemporal memory
status_evidence.snippet: PDE models incorporating spatial memory have been developed, but the precise transport terms reflecting memory effects remain unclear.
status_evidence.claim: PDE memory modeling is active and unresolved, supporting open status.
